also: how am I supposed to know?

terms.grammar: deliberative subjunctive: “how am I to know?”
evidence: Traupman 35: how should I know?, quōmodo sciam?
terms.comment: The subjunctive makes the question a protest, as in Quid faciam?, what am I to do?. Lewis & Short does not quote this question; it has Quī scīs?, how do you know? (Plaut. Ep. 2.2.65).

phrases.latin: Ubi sunt calceī meī? — Quōmodo sciam?
phrases.english: Where are my shoes? — How should I know?

sources: Lewis & Short: scio
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 35, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
